name: P-ONE
summary: A Canadian deep-Pacific neutrino-telescope project uses Ocean Networks Canada infrastructure to expand Northern Hemisphere coverage for high-energy astronomy.
physics_targets: Neutrino source localisation and multimessenger observation
detection_principle: Instrumented mooring lines carry optical and calibration modules that measure Cherenkov photons in deep seawater. Existing cabled ocean infrastructure provides power and communication.

sites.name: Canada; Cascadia Basin in the northeastern Pacific, off British Columbia
sites.location: Canada; Cascadia Basin in the northeastern Pacific, off British Columbia

status.label: Under construction
status.evidence: The project describes advanced construction and completed first-line integration; the first-line page still phrases 2026 deployment as the next milestone.

timeline.event: STRAW and STRAW-b pathfinders characterised the optical environment.
First-line integration completed; deployment was scheduled for 2026 on the project site.

results.summary: Deep-sea site and optical-background measurements support the detector design; a scheduled line deployment is not treated as completion of the full array.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
